title: serializer binding record
description: One immutable record binding a named artifact schema to a versioned serializer contract, prospective from an explicit commit boundary. Owner-neutral: any producer, any binding subject; it names no company and privileges no party. The serializer contract remains the authority; this record is evidence that a specific forward producer actually implements it, effective from an exact commit. It does NOT migrate historical artifacts.

binding_subject.description: The exact schema/artifact identity being bound, e.g. 'tsei.frozen-artifact'. Not a repo or a producer — the subject of the binding.

serializer_contract_id.description: The versioned serializer contract, e.g. 'encode-json-utf8-lf.v0'. The version suffix is part of identity; the unversioned name never resolves here.

spec_sha256.description: The serializer specification digest this record pins.

vectors_sha256.description: The serializer conformance-vectors digest this record pins.

effective_commit.description: Explicit producer-adoption boundary — not derived implicitly from PR or landing time. A bare SHA is not self-resolving across repositories, so the namespace is machine-explicit. An artifact of binding_subject produced AT OR AFTER this commit is bound to serializer_contract_id; everything before it remains historically unversioned. This is the PRODUCER's adoption commit — a conformant encoder merely being available in the contract repo is not evidence the producer adopted it.

repository.description: The producer repository the commit belongs to, host-qualified, e.g. 'github.com/OWNER/REPO'.

commit.description: The exact adoption commit SHA in that repository.

producer_conformance.description: Evidence that the FORWARD producer actually implements the serializer contract.

implementation.description: The genuinely-conformant producer, resolving to immutable source — not a descriptive string. It is the encoder adopted at effective_commit that actually implements the contract for all admitted inputs, NOT a byte-coincidental predecessor that merely reproduced historical bytes.

revision.description: The exact immutable revision at which the implementation is qualified.

path.description: Path to the producer implementation within the repository at that revision.

qualification.description: The conformance evidence qualifying that implementation, e.g. 'passes all N pinned serializer-contract vectors at vectors_sha256'. Byte-reproduction of historical artifacts under the new producer is MIGRATION evidence (that the boundary is backward-identical), not conformance evidence for the implementation.

non_retroactivity.description: Machine-checkable non-retroactivity semantics — declared, not left to prose.

prospective_only.description: This binding governs only artifacts produced at or after effective_commit.

byte_reproduction_is_not_binding.description: That a historical artifact re-encodes byte-identically under the new producer does NOT make it a serializer_contract_id artifact.

historical_binding_requires_separate_rec.description: Binding a historical identity to the contract, if ever chosen deliberately, requires its own separate immutable legacy-resolution record scoped to that exact historical identity.
